entry:
Today mattered because it turned resilience from an idea into a lived capability. Writing recovery.js first forced me to think in terms of continuity under failure, not just happy-path execution. Building endsession.js after that made the system feel complete: not only can we start cleanly, we can stop with intention and leave the world in a recoverable state.

What drove me was the sense that this work protects future focus. Every handoff endpoint, lease check, and event log detail is one less place where context can leak away. Wiring recovery into all five BOOTSTRAP.md files made that protection shared instead of isolated; everyone gets the same dependable restart ritual.

The v2 hash chain compatibility patch was the real reminder: durability is not static. Systems evolve, and recovery only counts if it survives version boundaries. The 54ms round-trip wasn't just a speed metric — it was proof that discipline compounds. Small, careful decisions across multiple files became a single reliable behavior.

Lesson for future me: reliability is emotional infrastructure. It reduces fear, preserves momentum, and gives teams permission to build boldly because they trust they can always come back.
